variants.title: Variants
variants.desc: A variant decides how loud a component is — how much surface it claims and how it separates from what is behind it. Intent decides what it means; variant decides how much it insists.
variants.vocab_desc: These four names are common across component libraries. WIM UI does not expose all four everywhere — see the next section for what each family actually accepts.
variants.solid_look: Filled with the intent colour, text in the on-colour
variants.solid_use: The one action a screen is built around. More than one solid per screen and none of them reads as primary.
variants.outline_look: A 1px border in the intent colour
variants.outline_use: Shows structure without claiming attention. Secondary actions, and anything that should read as a bounded region.
variants.subtle_look: A light tint of the intent colour, no border
variants.subtle_use: Elements that repeat. Twenty outlined tags become twenty competing rectangles; twenty tinted ones read as one soft mass and let the text carry the meaning.
variants.ghost_look: Transparent at rest, background on hover
variants.ghost_use: Controls that live inside other chrome — toolbar icons, list row actions — where a resting border would add a second grid.
variants.families_desc: The vocabulary is split per family, and the splits are deliberate.
variants.why_no_subtle: Buttons have no `subtle`. A button must look pressable, and a tint without a border reads as a label rather than a control. Where a quieter button is wanted, `ghost` fills that role.
variants.why_no_ghost: Indicators have no `ghost`. A badge that is transparent at rest and only appears on hover is not a badge — indicators are read, not operated, so there is nothing to reveal on hover.
variants.outline_desc: The background behind an outline differs by family, and it is not an oversight. Two of the three have a hard constraint, and they pull in opposite directions.
variants.outline_field: Opaque. A field is a surface you type onto; if the page shows through, the value becomes unreadable.
variants.outline_indicator: Transparent. Badges and tags sit inside alerts, on tinted rows, over coloured panels. An opaque badge would float above whatever it is placed on.
variants.outline_button: Opaque. Buttons have no constraint either way, so this one is a choice: an opaque surface guarantees the text contrast regardless of what the button is placed on.
variants.outline_note: Because the constraints point in opposite directions, there is no single definition of `outline` that serves all three. This page records the difference rather than papering over it.
variants.measured_desc: The tint is 13% of the intent colour. The workable range is narrow: below 12% the fill stops being distinguishable from the surface, and above 15% the text drops under WCAG AA. Adding a border to compensate turns it back into `outline`; adding a shadow breaks the one-elevation-per-screen rule.
variants.intents_link: Intent decides what a component means; this page is about how loudly it says it. The intent vocabulary has its own page.
